claims.text: Bulk (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 is susceptible to cracking under load and has poor mechanical integrity.
The untreated alloy has moderate caloric performance.
Melt spinning at a cooling rate above 10^5 K/s will produce nanocrystalline (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 ribbons.
A short anneal at 500–600 °C will control grain growth after melt spinning.
The proposed processing will create submicron to near-nanometer grains with clean, well-controlled grain boundaries.
Grain refinement will increase yield strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Grain refinement will increase crack resistance.
Excessive grain refinement would cause inverse Hall–Petch softening in this alloy.
The short annealing treatment will keep grain sizes above the threshold for inverse Hall–Petch softening.
The refined microstructure and annealing treatment will preserve the caloric phase transformation.
The treatment will improve compressive strength by at least 30% and potentially by 30–50% relative to the unrefined alloy.
After treatment, caloric entropy change will remain within 95–105% of that of the unrefined alloy.
Applied magnetic-field and pressure-field operation from ambient temperature to approximately 400 °C represents the previously used operating regime.
The proposed treatment must not change the alloy composition or introduce rare-earth elements.
Failure to obtain at least a 30% compressive-strength improvement, or a caloric entropy change within ±5% of the untreated value, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The task describes the unchanged alloy as providing a large caloric response, whereas the baseline characterizes its caloric performance as moderate.
